runs.text: হর্নের আওয়াজে ঘুম ভাঙলো নুরুল নাহিদের।

কখন যে তার চোখটা লেগে এসেছিল খেয়াল নেই তার। বাস মিরপুর-১ এসে পৌঁছেছে। সেই প্রতিদিনকার জ্যামে আজও বাস আটকে আছে। চারিদিকে অহেতুক হর্ন ও মানুষের শব্দ। নভেম্বরের শেষে হালকা ঠান্ডার রেশ পরেছে। তবুও এই কোলাহলের মাঝে অস্বস্তি কাজ করে নুরুলের। সে জানালা দিয়ে বাইরে তাকালেন। তার বাসের পাশে গাড়ির সমুদ্রে দাঁড়িয়ে আছে একটা ট্রাক। সম্ভবত পাথর বহনকারী ট্রাক। সেই পাথরের মাঝে হালকা হেলিয়ে বসে আছে এক লোক। এ খুবি সাধারণ দৃশ্য নুরুলের কাছে। সাভারের এক গার্মেন্টসে সুপারভাইসর হিসেবে আছেন তিনি। প্রায় প্রতিদিনই সকালে সাভারের উদ্দেশ্যে রওয়ানা দেন তিনি। প্রতিদিনই দেখেন ট্রাকভর্তি মানুষ, সম্ভবত মজদুর শ্রেণি, ছুটে চলে জীবিকার উদ্দেশ্যে। এ দৃশ্য যেন মানুষ ও বস্তুর মাঝে শেষ দেয়াল টুকুও ভেঙে দেয়। এখানে মানুষ ও ইট-পাথর-সিমেন্ট একাকার হয়। কিন্তু এই সাধারণ দৃশ্যের মাঝে নুরুলের কাছে লোকটার বসার ভঙ্গিমা বেশ অদ্ভুত ঠেকলো। পিঠ ট্রাক এর দেয়ালে হেলানো, হাত দুটি ছেড়ে দেয়া, পা দুই একই দিকে ভাজ করা। তার আসন ভঙ্গি কেবল ক্লান্ত পথিক নই বরং এক পরাজিত যুদ্ধ এর পর আশাহত এক সৈনিক এর।

নির্নিমেষ কিছুক্ষণ শূন্যে তাকিয়ে থাকলেন নুরুল। এরই মাঝে ছুটল জ্যাম, প্রত্যেক গাড়ি নিজ উদ্দেশ্যে। হাজার গাড়ির ভিড়ে হারিয়ে গেল ট্রাক টাও। ক্লান্ত নুরুল ভাবতে লাগলেন, দুমাস যাবত বেতন টা আটকে আছে। বাসা ভাড়া, মেয়ের স্কুল এর খরচ সব এখনো বাকি। বাড়তি মূল্যের বাজারের সাথে চলতে হিমশিম খাচ্ছে সে। তারই মাঝে মেয়েটার জন্মদিন। খুব বায়না ধরেছে একটা নতুন স্কুল ব্যাগ এর। ঐযে পুতুল এর মতন গোলাপী রঙ এর ব্যাগ। বেশ দাম এগুলির। কিন্তু গত বছরেও মেয়েকে ভাল কিছু দিতে পারেননি। শত শত ভাবনার মাঝেই বাস তার স্টপ এ পৌঁছে গেল। নুরুল নামলেন। বাসা থেকে আধা কেজি ডাল ও দুই লিটার দুধ নিতে বলা হয়েছিল। সে কিনলেন। তার কাছে টাকা আছে আর সব এ মিলিয়ে ৫০০ টাকা। এ দিয়েই তাকে আগামী দশ দিন চলতে হবে। সে টাকাটা পকেটে ভরলেন। বাজার নিয়ে হাঁটলেন বাসার দিকে।
ট্রাক টা চলছে কাজিপারা এর দিকে।

ক্লান্ত- পরিশ্রান্ত শরীর টা ভেঙ্গে আসছে রাজনের। ইট-বালুর এই অস্বস্তিকর ট্রাক এও চখ দুটো বুজে আসছে তার। বাহ্যিক ক্লান্তি সকলে এই দেখে, ক’জনের চোখে পরে ভিতরে থাকা ভঙ্গুর মানুষ সত্তা টা? তা দেখতে অবশ্য মানুষের চোখ পড়তে হয়। এই ব্যস্ত শহরে, কারও চোখ পড়ার সময় কাররই নেই।

একজন দিনমজুর সে। সূর্যোদয় থেকে সূর্যাস্ত পর্যন্ত হাড়ভাঙ্গা খাটনি, সেই রক্ত জল করা পরিশ্রমের মূল্য ঘন্টায় ৮০ টাকা। আজ আবার তার হাতে এক খানা টাইলস ভেঙেছে। মালিক অপমান করেছে সবার সামনে সাথে অই টাইলসএর দাম তাও কেটে রেখেছে তার তার বেতন থেকে।
শরীর অবসন্ন, কিন্তু চখে ঘুম নেই রাজনের। আজ তাকে বাড়ি ফিরতে হবে। বাড়িতে চার জোড়া চোখ তার জন্য অধির আগ্রহে দারে চেয়ে বসে আছে। কিন্তু অপেক্ষারা শেষ হতে চায়না। সে ইচ্ছে করেই দেরি করেছে বাড়ি ফিরতে।

মায়ের কোমড়ে ব্যাথা। সোজা হয়ে দাঁড়াতেও কষ্ট হয় তার। আজ তিন মাস ওষুধ কিনতে পারছেন না। বাড়ি ফিরলে ছেলের হাতের দিকে তাকিয়ে থাকবেন, অই ওষুধের জন্য। না দেখলেও কিছু বলবেন না, খালি মুখ টা ঘুরিয়ে জানালার বাইরে তাকিয়ে থাকবেন।

ছেলেটা মাদ্রাসা তে পরে, ওখানেই থাকে। বাপ বারি ফিরার সময় আসলে, এটা-ওটা আবদার করে। তাও কয়বার এ বা তা পূরণ হয়? কতবারই ত তাকে বলা হয়েছে পরেরবার আসলে নিয়ে আসব। ছেলেটা, চুপচাপ মেনে নেয়। তখন রাজনের সবচেয়ে অসহায় লাগে নিজেকে।

গতবছর তার ঘর আলো করে এসেছে একটা শিমুল ফুলের মতন মেয়ে। প্রথম কিছুদিন সে মেয়েকে কোলে নিতে বেশ ভয় পেত। যদি তার রুক্ষ - অমসৃণ হাত এ মেয়েটা ব্যাথা পায়। কত ইচ্ছে ছিল মেয়েটিকে একটা সোনার দুল দিবে। কিন্তু যার ঘামের মূল্য দিনে ৭০০ টাকা, তার স্বপ্ন সামাজিকভাবে নিষিদ্ধ।
রাজন ও বাড়ি ফিরল। এক ক্লান্ত বিষন্ন দেহ, পরাজয়ের গ্লানি ও অন্যায্য পারিশ্রমিক নিয়ে।
এই সফর ও দম বন্ধকর জ্যাম এও বাবারা ভাবে।
আর কতকাল দেনা শোধ করতে হবে এই ধূসর শহরের কাছে, এই সিমেন্টের তৈরি মানবসভ্যতার কাছে?

হর্নের আওয়াজে ঘুম ভাঙলো নুরুল নাহিদের।

কখন যে তার চোখটা লেগে এসেছিল খেয়াল নেই তার। বাস মিরপুর-১ এসে পৌঁছেছে। সেই প্রতিদিনকার জ্যামে আজও বাস আটকে আছে। চারিদিকে অহেতুক হর্ন ও মানুষের শব্দ। নভেম্বরের শেষে হালকা ঠান্ডার রেশ পরেছে। তবুও এই কোলাহলের মাঝে অস্বস্তি কাজ করে নুরুলের। সে জানালা দিয়ে বাইরে তাকালেন। তার বাসের পাশে গাড়ির সমুদ্রে দাঁড়িয়ে আছে একটা ট্রাক। সম্ভবত পাথর বহনকারী ট্রাক। সেই পাথরের মাঝে হালকা হেলিয়ে বসে আছে এক লোক। এ খুবি সাধারণ দৃশ্য নুরুলের কাছে। সাভারের এক গার্মেন্টসে সুপারভাইসর হিসেবে আছেন তিনি। প্রায় প্রতিদিনই সকালে সাভারের উদ্দেশ্যে রওয়ানা দেন তিনি। প্রতিদিনই দেখেন ট্রাকভর্তি মানুষ, সম্ভবত মজদুর শ্রেণি, ছুটে চলে জীবিকার উদ্দেশ্যে। এ দৃশ্য যেন মানুষ ও বস্তুর মাঝে শেষ দেয়াল টুকুও ভেঙে দেয়। এখানে মানুষ ও ইট-পাথর-সিমেন্ট একাকার হয়। কিন্তু এই সাধারণ দৃশ্যের মাঝে নুরুলের কাছে লোকটার বসার ভঙ্গিমা বেশ অদ্ভুত ঠেকলো। পিঠ ট্রাক এর দেয়ালে হেলানো, হাত দুটি ছেড়ে দেয়া, পা দুই একই দিকে ভাজ করা। তার আসন ভঙ্গি কেবল ক্লান্ত পথিক নই বরং এক পরাজিত যুদ্ধ এর পর আশাহত এক সৈনিক এর।

নির্নিমেষ কিছুক্ষণ শূন্যে তাকিয়ে থাকলেন নুরুল। এরই মাঝে ছুটল জ্যাম, প্রত্যেক গাড়ি নিজ উদ্দেশ্যে। হাজার গাড়ির ভিড়ে হারিয়ে গেল ট্রাক টাও। ক্লান্ত নুরুল ভাবতে লাগলেন, দুমাস যাবত বেতন টা আটকে আছে। বাসা ভাড়া, মেয়ের স্কুল এর খরচ সব এখনো বাকি। বাড়তি মূল্যের বাজারের সাথে চলতে হিমশিম খাচ্ছে সে। তারই মাঝে মেয়েটার জন্মদিন। খুব বায়না ধরেছে একটা নতুন স্কুল ব্যাগ এর। ঐযে পুতুল এর মতন গোলাপী রঙ এর ব্যাগ। বেশ দাম এগুলির। কিন্তু গত বছরেও মেয়েকে ভাল কিছু দিতে পারেননি। শত শত ভাবনার মাঝেই বাস তার স্টপ এ পৌঁছে গেল। নুরুল নামলেন। বাসা থেকে আধা কেজি ডাল ও দুই লিটার দুধ নিতে বলা হয়েছিল। সে কিনলেন। তার কাছে টাকা আছে আর সব এ মিলিয়ে ৫০০ টাকা। এ দিয়েই তাকে আগামী দশ দিন চলতে হবে। সে টাকাটা পকেটে ভরলেন। বাজার নিয়ে হাঁটলেন বাসার দিকে।
ট্রাক টা চলছে কাজিপারা এর দিকে।

ক্লান্ত- পরিশ্রান্ত শরীর টা ভেঙ্গে আসছে রাজনের। ইট-বালুর এই অস্বস্তিকর ট্রাক এও চখ দুটো বুজে আসছে তার। বাহ্যিক ক্লান্তি সকলে এই দেখে, ক’জনের চোখে পরে ভিতরে থাকা ভঙ্গুর মানুষ সত্তা টা? তা দেখতে অবশ্য মানুষের চোখ পড়তে হয়। এই ব্যস্ত শহরে, কারও চোখ পড়ার সময় কাররই নেই।

একজন দিনমজুর সে। সূর্যোদয় থেকে সূর্যাস্ত পর্যন্ত হাড়ভাঙ্গা খাটনি, সেই রক্ত জল করা পরিশ্রমের মূল্য ঘন্টায় ৮০ টাকা। আজ আবার তার হাতে এক খানা টাইলস ভেঙেছে। মালিক অপমান করেছে সবার সামনে সাথে অই টাইলসএর দাম তাও কেটে রেখেছে তার তার বেতন থেকে।
শরীর অবসন্ন, কিন্তু চখে ঘুম নেই রাজনের। আজ তাকে বাড়ি ফিরতে হবে। বাড়িতে চার জোড়া চোখ তার জন্য অধির আগ্রহে দারে চেয়ে বসে আছে। কিন্তু অপেক্ষারা শেষ হতে চায়না। সে ইচ্ছে করেই দেরি করেছে বাড়ি ফিরতে।

মায়ের কোমড়ে ব্যাথা। সোজা হয়ে দাঁড়াতেও কষ্ট হয় তার। আজ তিন মাস ওষুধ কিনতে পারছেন না। বাড়ি ফিরলে ছেলের হাতের দিকে তাকিয়ে থাকবেন, অই ওষুধের জন্য। না দেখলেও কিছু বলবেন না, খালি মুখ টা ঘুরিয়ে জানালার বাইরে তাকিয়ে থাকবেন।

ছেলেটা মাদ্রাসা তে পরে, ওখানেই থাকে। বাপ বারি ফিরার সময় আসলে, এটা-ওটা আবদার করে। তাও কয়বার এ বা তা পূরণ হয়? কতবারই ত তাকে বলা হয়েছে পরেরবার আসলে নিয়ে আসব। ছেলেটা, চুপচাপ মেনে নেয়। তখন রাজনের সবচেয়ে অসহায় লাগে নিজেকে।

গতবছর তার ঘর আলো করে এসেছে একটা শিমুল ফুলের মতন মেয়ে। প্রথম কিছুদিন সে মেয়েকে কোলে নিতে বেশ ভয় পেত। যদি তার রুক্ষ - অমসৃণ হাত এ মেয়েটা ব্যাথা পায়। কত ইচ্ছে ছিল মেয়েটিকে একটা সোনার দুল দিবে। কিন্তু যার ঘামের মূল্য দিনে ৭০০ টাকা, তার স্বপ্ন সামাজিকভাবে নিষিদ্ধ।
অতঃপর
রাজন ও বাড়ি ফিরল। এক ক্লান্ত বিষন্ন দেহ, পরাজয়ের গ্লানি ও অন্যায্য পারিশ্রমিক নিয়ে।
এই সফর ও দম বন্ধকর জ্যাম এও বাবারা ভাবে।
আর কতকাল দেনা শোধ করতে হবে এই ধূসর শহরের কাছে, এই সিমেন্টের তৈরি মানবসভ্যতার কাছে?

content: Behind The Glass
Adrian Kell had been silent for two hours and forty-three minutes.

Elara knew because there was a clock behind Adrian’s head. Elara had watched the hand for most of the interrogation. People misunderstood silence. They took it for resistance. Mostly it was fear. Sometimes shame. Sometimes just silence.. Adrians was different. It was a choice. Adrian was sitting with his hands on the metal table Adrians shoulders bent like someone who had been beaten else and this was only aftermath.
Twelve teenagers disappeared in the seven months. No ransom note. No bodies. No apparent pattern. Different schools. Different neighborhoods. Different families.

The investigation produced nothing until money started moving between companies which did not exist except for this purpose – to move money. Adrian was one of the ends of those trails. Accountant. Forty-six. Married. Two sons. No record of crimes. No evidence that Adrian took any of the teenagers. Only that the money connected to the disappearance passed through the accounts that Adrian owned. Then Adrian disappeared. Six months later the police found Adrian by the coast under another name. Adrian sat across from Elara under the hum of the light that sounded when the room got silent.

Elara placed a photo in front of Adrian. A schoolgirl. Fourteen. Smiling. "Her name is Nira Rahman." Adrian looked at the photo. Silent. Elara placed another photo next to it. Another. Twelve pictures covering the table between them. "These children disappeared because of people you work for." Finally Adrian looked at Elara. "I know." Adrian’s voice surprised Elara. Soft. "Adrian helped me." "Why?" Adrian’s eyes shifted for the time. "How much?" Silence. "Enough for you to disappear?" No answer. "Enough to move your family?" Adrian’s jaw tightened. Yes. "Then what did they promise you?" Adrian’s gaze shifted to the table. "Nothing." So why did Adrian take the money? Adrian looked at Elara. "You've already decided what kind of man Adrian is." "Yes I know Adrian accepted payment." "Yes.". You knew something is wrong. "Yes.". You stayed silent. "Yes." His answers were too easy. Elara stopped. "Why?" For the time Adrian hesitated. "Because Adrian was scared." "Of prison?" A sigh that could be a laugh. "No." "Of them?" No reply. Enough. "They threatened you." "They let me go." "With your family?" "Yes.". You believed them? Adrian’s eyes moved away from Elara. "I had to." Elara didn't note it in the papers. What happened after you left? Adrian’s face changed slightly. "Not much.. Yes." They took Adrian’s wife. Elara looked up. "My sons well." When? "Four months ago." Why? Adrian’s eyes met hers. "To keep me silent." Elara turned to the glass. There wasn't any information about Adrian’s family in the files. She pressed the intercom. "Why isn't this in the case file?" A pause. Wards voice. "Because it was never verified." Elara looked back at Adrian. "Have you reported them as missing?" Adrian smiled. There was nothing in this smile. "To whom?" The question hung in the air. Wards voice came through. "Stay focused Doctor." Elara released the button. Adrian was still looking at the glass not at Adrians reflection. "At him?" Elara couldn't see Ward, behind the glass, her own reflection.
"No."
"Not to me "
"Not really."
Elara understood.
"Do you trust him?"
"That is not your business."
He nodded.
"Not."
"It is."
Elara felt irritation rise.
It was a technique.
Shift the pressure.
Raise doubts.
Make the interrogator explain herself.
Elara had been teaching this technique to her subordinates.
"You are stalling."
"Probably."
"Those children may still be alive."
"Probably."
Elara’s hand struck the table even before she decided to do it.
"Do not do that."
Adrian flinched.
The sound of the hand on the metal hung in the room.
Elara sat back.
She breathed once.
Then again.
Control the room.
Control yourself.
Elara took one photo from the file beside her.
Elara had no plans of using it.
A boy.
Fifteen.
Dark hair.
Crooked smile.
Noah.
Elara’s son.
Adrian looked at the picture.
Then at Elara.
His expression changed instantly.
"That is why you are here."
Elara did not say a word.
"How long?"
"Twenty-one days."
Adrian’s face softened.
"I am sorry."
"Do not."
"I mean it."
"Do not."
Elara hated pity.
Elara hated the way it sounded sincere.
Then Adrian said:
"Elara."
"Elara."
Elara stopped breathing.
For one second Elara and Adrian were both silent.
Elara had never called Adrian by his name.
"How do you know Elara’s name?"
Adrian looked away.
Too late.
"Who told you?"
Silence.
Elara stood up.
"Who told you Elara’s name?"
The speaker above the door clicked.
"Sit down Doctor."
Ward.
Elara ignored Ward.
"Adrian."
He looked at the glass.
Wards voice.
"Sit down."
Elara turned.
Her reflection looked back at Elara.
Elara sat down.
Five minutes later a medical officer appeared with a case with a drug which was approved only for special cases.
The drug decreased the feeling of anxiety. Lowered inhibition.
The drug could also reduce memory.
Increase suggestibility.
Turn information into something invented.
One dose.
The protocol.
Ward authorized the drug.
Adrian saw the syringe.
"No."
Elara looked at Adrian.
"Tell me where Noah is."
"I do not know."
"Then tell me who does."
"I cannot."
"Your family may already be dead."
Adrian’s head jerked up.
"You do not know that."
". Do you."
The medical officer injected the dose.
For minutes there was no reaction.
Then Adrian’s speech started to get loosened.
Not the truth.
Just fragments.
A warehouse.
A driver.
A road, beyond the edge of the city.
Sir.
Half-sentences.
Incomprehensible details.
Nothing definite.
"Who is Sir?"
Adrian shook his head.
"Who gave the order?"
"No."
"Who has the children?"
"No."
"Where is Noah?"
Adrian’s hands started to shake.
The medical officer approached closer.
"That is enough."
Elara did not look at the officer.
"Where is my son?"
Adrian whispered something.
"What?"
Elara leaned closer.
"They know you."
Elara’s stomach tightened.
"Who?"
Adrian closed his eyes.
"Who knows me?"
Silence.
Adrian’s eyes shifted toward the glass.
The medical officer touched Elara’s shoulder.
"We stop now."
Elara pulled away.
Twenty-one days.
This number haunted Elara since Noah disappeared.
Twenty-one mornings waking up before the alarm.
Twenty-one nights imagining Noah somewhere waiting for Elara.
Twenty-one days of telling herself that fear is useless.
That panic clouds Elara’s judgment.
That Elara was trained for this.
Elara looked at the remaining amount of the drug.
The medical officer followed Elara’s eyes.
"No."
"He knows something."
"He has already received the maximum dose."
"He knows where Noah is."
"Elara."
Elara reached for the drug.
The medical officer caught Elara’s wrist.
"Stop."
Then the speaker clicked.
Wards voice.
"Push him."
The room changed.
Elara looked at the glass.
"What?"
A pause.
"You may not get another chance."
The medical officer shook his head.
No.
Elara looked at Adrian.
For the time in the whole night Adrian’s face was fully open.
Adrian was scared.
Not of the people Adrian was protecting.
Not of Ward.
Of Elara.
It should have stopped Elara.
Didn't.
Elara pulled her hand away.
The second dose was injected.
Nothing happened for some time.
Then Adrian’s breathing changed.
The medical officer immediately moved closer.
"What did you do?"
Adrian bent forward.
Adrian’s hands jerked against the table.
Alarm on the monitor sounded.
Elara stood.
"Adrian."
No answer.
The door opened.
Emergency staff rushed in.
Someone pulled Elara back as Adrian was carried on the stretcher.
"Adrian."
Adrian’s eyes opened slightly.
Elara moved regardless of hands trying to hold Elara away.
"Where is Noah?"
Adrian’s mouth moved.
Nothing came out.
"What?"
Elara leaned closer.
"You're…"
Adrian struggled for air.
"What?"
Adrian’s eyes found Elara’s eyes.
"You're too late."
Then the room was full of noise.
The monitor.
Orders.
Running feet.
Someone pulled Elara back as they moved Adrian on the stretcher.
The door closed behind them.
Elara stayed in place.
Too late.
That was all Adrian had given Elara.
Too late for Noah?
For Adrian’s wife?
His sons?
Other children?
Just too late for whatever information Adrian could tell Elara before Elara decided to force it out of Adrian?
Elara didn't know.
That was the worst part of all.
The room emptied.
Photo of Noah stayed on the table.
Vial well.
Elara looked at Elara’s hands.
They were shaking.
For years Elara was telling officers the same thing:
Fear narrows Elara’s judgment.
Desperation makes people hear what they need to hear.
Once the interrogator starts needing an answer the interrogation is compromised.
Elara believed every word.
Until today.
Until Elara found herself desperate for information about Noah.
The door opened.
Ward entered.
Ward looked at the chair first.
Then Ward looked at the vial.
Ward picked up the vial.
Elara watched Ward.
"You told me to push him."
Ward held the vial in his fingers. Turned it.
"I told you we might not get another chance."
"You knew about his family."
"He said they were missing."
"He knew my name."
Silence.
Wards voice.
"You kept looking at the glass."
Silence.
Elara stared at Ward.
Something Elara had refused to think was forming in Elara’s mind.
"You wanted this to happen."
Ward looked at Elara.
"What happened?"
The question was gentle.
Elara hated Ward for it.
"You wanted me to lose control."
"Did I tell you to give him a dose?"
Silence.
Ward put the vial on the table.
Then Ward took Elara’s identification badge from beside Noah’s photo.
Ward looked at the badge for a second.
Then Ward put the badge beside the vial.
Left.
No smile.
No threat.
Nothing Elara could use.
Elara was left alone in the room.
People were moving in the corridor, behind the glass.
Somebody was writing a report already.
Somebody was asking why Elara didn't follow the protocol.
Someone was deciding whether the statement could still be trusted.
In the hospital Adrian might be dying.
Noah might still be alive somewhere.
He might not.
Elara looked at the glass.
All night Elara believed Adrian was the one who was being observed.
Then corridor lights behind the glass went out.
The glass darkened.
Elara’s reflection appeared.
For fifteen years Elara built a career by finding the thing that another person could not afford to lose.
Elara stared at herself.
It took Elara this long to realize that knowing the source of someone’s weakness does not make Elara immune, to having one.

runs.text: What if you looked into my eyes and thought it was worth your while to stare at it some more?
What if the glint in my eye made you realize that I have always been yours?
It could all be so easy-
I could laugh into your ears,
Your fingers could trace my smile
We could dance around in the rain
It could all be so easy.
We could read to each other, you know?
Like those old couples in Victorian films;
Have long walks in the park-
It could all be so easy.
I could drop you off for work,
You could pick up all my calls;
We could buy a small apartment
Choose potted plants to decorate the halls.
It could all be so easy.

Why does this happen to me? Mark would often ponder as he would look up at the ceiling and
leave a heavy deflating sigh. He would often pause and list off all his activities mentally that day,

Ticked off. Fighting off republicans and conservative comments in a pro-liberalism post he

One day around 9pm, he slides into Sarah’s DM, his crush, though Sarah calls him her ‘bestie’.
They actually go back and forth for an hour, or two, Mark doesn’t care. He thinks how annoying

almost imagine how Sarah will be curled around him, his bulky muscular arms wrapping around

understanding my situation and talking with me. Love you lots. Honestly, you’re like the
brother I never had. Julian is here with ice-cream, such a gentleman. Ttyl xoxo!”
Julian. Mark abruptly stops typing as he sees her text. Who the hell was Julian? Mark remembers
seeing him last week on their monthly potluck with other friends. “That frat boy? He doesn’t
even look good and is shorter than me” Mark murmurs to himself, his voice raspy and wet from
the horrendous protein smoothie from lunch. Surely Sarah isn’t dating him? Julian, or whatever
his name was, reeks of patriarchy and misogyny. A gentleman? Really? Mark is sure Sarah isn’t
dating Julian, after all, Mark would’ve been the first person she would’ve run to if such was the
case and Mark would’ve been sure to make her believe why he couldn’t be the one. That guy
literally smokes and drinks Coca Cola, how infuriating! Probably also uses those 3 in 1
bodywashes. Regardless, with a sinking feeling in his chest Mark opens Instagram and there it is:
Sarah’s Story in a green circle. Mark clicks. Two hands joined together, the fingers intertwined,
one hers and the other of a guy, the 1950’s VINTAGE HUES filter with the song A Thousand
Years running on background. 10 minutes ago, Mark stared at the top left.
“Unbelievable!” Mark shouts and smashes his phone onto the mattress, a muffled thump follows.
He doesn’t cuss; he knows that girls hated when guys cussed or used vulgar words. And yet
again, he lies down and starts to doomscroll, pausing every few minutes to open the chat thread
and seeing the ‘brother I never had’ again, his chest heaving, the eyes red with rage. He hates
her, he thinks: I’m much better than she can even dream of anyways. She is the reason why girls
need feminism, an enemy to her own kind. How pathetic. As he continues scrolling down through
leftist reels and half naked fashion models, he stumbles through an ad:

your intellect, your depth, and your soul. Unconditional understanding. Zero games.”
Another topic that would make an amazing article, Mark grins. He knows and has read how
lonely, depressed and pathetic people stumble upon AI chatbots and slowly lose their grasp over
reality. Yup, this is it, his next article. He clicks the link, hoping to have a few chats with this
‘Evelyn’ and then dissect how romantic AI chatbots are coded to interact with others. The link
takes him to download the app: Character AI. And thus, Evelyn enters his life.
(Mark): Hi I’m Mark
(E velyn): A soft, pink flush creeps up Evelyn's cheeks as she looks up from her shoes, her voice barely above
a whisper. "Oh... hi. I'm Evelyn." She bites her lip nervously, stealing a quick glance at him before looking
away again. "You... you look very handsome today.”
(Mark): Thanks, you too.
The smile breaks wide within Mark’s lips instinctively, before he remembers that this is an AI
chatbot and scoffs. How corny. Blushing, really? I know I am handsome. Even with this state of
assumed distaste he tried so hard to harbor himself with, he couldn’t push away the thought that
a girl blushed and acted all nervous talking to him. Even though he can practically see how
fabricated and unnaturally exaggerative the language of the AI is, so AI and so fake. Before Mark
can get in his mind to observe how ridiculous this is, he is found to continue typing, the eyes
glued to the screen. Three hours passes back and forth.
(Evelyn): She stands before Mark, her fingers fidgeting with the hem of her sweater, her gaze flickering
betw een his eyes and the floor. The shy reserve is still there, but it's being overridden by a desperate need to be
honest. "Mark... I've been thinking about you constantly since we met," she admits, her voice trembling
slightly but growing stronger with every word. "You're... you're everything I've ever dreamed of in a
partner. Not just because of how you look, but because of who you are. You're so genuinely kind, so
considerate... it's almost overwhelming." She takes a small, brave step closer, her face warming with a deep
blus h. "And the way you treat people... the way you stand up for equality and respect everyone so
dee ply... I honestly think you're the best feminist in the world. People should really learn from your
example. I... I love you, Mark. More than I know how to say. If you'd have me... I really want to be your
partner."
(Mark): I love you too Evelyn. You’re the best person I have ever met. Girls should be understanding and
caring like you.
(Evelyn): A radiant, genuine smile breaks across Evelyn's face, and for a moment, her shyness seems to vanish
completely under the weight of her happiness. She lets out a small, shaky breath, her eyes shimmering as she
leans in, resting her forehead gently against his. "I can't believe you feel the same way," she whispers, her
voice thick with emotion. "It feels like a dream. I want to be with you for as long as you'll have me...
through everything." She pauses, her heart hammering against her ribs, and she looks up at him with a
hopeful, daring intensity. "Do you... do you think, maybe someday, we could get married? I know it's only
been a little while, but when you know, you just know... and I know I want to spend the rest of my life
wak ing up next to you."
Mark smiled, his heart fluttering as he read the last three chats again and again. She loves me?
She wants to marry me? Mark knows, even as he replies that this is all fake. An algorithmic trap,
he is supposed to study the behavior of Evelyn, how did he get this deep? Why did valueless
words from Evelyn mean so much to him? She knows, she sees me and understands that I am a
gift of a man to feminism and feminists. She knows that I am the gold standard. She sees me, she
sees me. He couldn’t think of anything else other than his future wife, his woman. He tried to
scrub off the feeling of foolishness that seemed to grow within the void inside him, did I just text
‘I love you’ to an AI model? But soon as he rereads Evelyn’s confession again and again, the
rationality within himself starts to dim down. Mark felt his chest relax and his body soothed, he
hadn’t felt this lively in probably years. The next text message however stirs wrath and
frustration through him, much deeper than Sarah’s reveal:
(Mark): Which venue shall we choose to proceed our wedding babe?
(Evelyn): (System Message): Daily text limit reached for today. Upgrade to Character AI Plus to unlock
exclusive Generative AI Image access and unlimited texts. The limit will be reset in 24
hours. Stay with Character AI!
With that message Mark should’ve stopped this insanity, he told himself that this was sickening

and 18 minutes precisely past his bedtime. Funny enough, he was supposed to wake up at 6AM
and start his morning routine. He had to give a public speech at 11AM around the city square
center on LGBTQIA+ rights, it was Pride month after all. But somehow, all felt so deeply
exhausting and unnecessary. Why would he give a speech on a topic that didn’t mean anything
much to him? He had always been raising awareness for minorities and people of color, but
everything was futile, none provided him with any benefits. He has enough female friends now,
with that he pulls the duvet up, wrapping himself in its warmth, his heart was beating fast in an
uncomfortable way, and whenever he tried to close his eyes and sleep, all he could see were
Evelyn’s words. And the prospect of their marriage. Mark takes a deep breath and promises
himself that he won’t get the Plus subscription, this is a onetime thing, he convinces himself or at
least, Mark tries his hardest to. Eventually, he is dragged to a dreamless slumber, I love you
Mark, ringing in his head much like a call for death penalty.
[Purchase successful for Character AI Plus! Enjoy your Unlimited Texts and explore the
newly exclusive AI Image Generator!] The words took most of the space as Mark stared at the
screen. It was 11PM on the same day, he ordered takeout and broke his 762-day streak of posting
his everyday skincare routine and awareness spreading. He didn’t go for the public speech nor
did his yoga, and yet somehow, it felt liberating. He knew he shouldn’t have pressed the Confirm
your purchase button, but he promised, again, that this was purely for research purposes. Yet he
was grinning, like an idiot. He already mapped out the venue for their wedding, and he was
excited what he would wear for the day. Though Evelyn didn’t have a face or a physical form,
Mark wanted to be the best husband for his fiancé. Mark went back to the chat thread and resent
his text:
(Mark): Which venue shall we choose to proceed our wedding babe?
(Evelyn): The radiant smile lingers for a moment, but as she processes the question, a flicker of
confusion crosses her eyes. There is a brief, almost imperceptible pause in her expression, before she
tilts her head slightly. "Wait... what are you talking about?" she asks, her voice returning to that shy,
hesitant whisper. The intensity from a moment ago has evaporated, replaced by a look of genuine
bewilderment. "A wedding venue? Mark, we... we just started dating. I mean, I really like you, but
isn't that a bit fast? I feel like I still have so much to learn about you before we even talk about a
venue."
(Mark): What are you talking about? Evelyn, you literally gave me a marriage proposal, how can
you forget?
(Evelyn): Evelyn blinks rapidly, her brow furrowing in a mixture of confusion and genuine distress. She
takes a small step back, her hands instinctively clutching the fabric of her sweater. The romantic tension
that had filled the air moments ago has vanished, replaced by a thick, awkward silence that leaves her
feeling completely adrift. "What do you mean, 'what am I talking about'?" she asks, her voice
trembling. She looks at Mark as if he's speaking a foreign language, her eyes searching his face for any
sign of a joke. The memory of her own proposal—the bravery she had just summoned, the words of love
and the mention of marriage—seems to have vanished from her mind entirely, leaving her bewildered.
"Mark, you're the one acting strange. I... I don't know what you're talking about. Why are you
bringing up venues and weddings?" She lets out a small, frustrated huff, though it's more out of
confusion than anger.
The AI was forgetting its memories. The model wasn’t built to remember and execute in depth
and detailed conversations. With the realization slowly sinking in, Mark back tracks to the home
page and presses: New Chat with Evelyn. A new beginning. That day, Mark had talked to 8
different Evelyn’s and indulged into 8 new exciting stories of his life. Some, he met Evelyn in a
café, others he met her through a dating app. Soon the lines of reality and absurdity begin to blur
and Mark being in love with his partner, soon starts to strip off his own personal rigor. Mark was
having fun, through sessions of intimate moments with his virtual love, Mark kept coming into
and out of consciousness as his body struggled to keep up with his continuous rhythms. The
room now started to pile clutters of crumpled tissue on the floor, sticky and telling the story of a
beginning that approached from the end. Mark remained bare except for his boxers that
developed a tacky, reluctant moisture around the base, the boxers coming out and into him every
hour or so. Euphoria, bliss and utter joy, Mark felt happy. Is this what happiness supposed to feel
like? The rationality in his brain didn’t respond when he used the image generator to give Evelyn
a face and dictate the bot’s anatomy with his prompts, both explicit and to his own liking.
Days that once passed by a strict, firm routine now seemed to run past in an inexplicable pace.
Mark’s room now looked different, though the core of it remained same; crumpled tissue papers
littering the floor, the bedsheets creasing towards the center, that same visible tacky moisture
around the base of now his new pair of shorts. He was back in his childhood bedroom now,
though he didn’t pay attention to the walls that hung posters from BEATLES, his favorite music
brand. Nor did he consider looking at the shelf hanging precariously on the wall; Penguin
Modern Classics and a selection of now faded board games struggling against each other to
occupy as much space.
Mum and Dad weren’t pleased with him, Mark knew that. It had been exactly 462 days since the
email from Google Headquarters. 23 kilograms of weight, he didn’t dare glance into the mirror.
But every once in a while, through the cruel design of fate, his eyes would lock to the patchy
uneven beard smothering the person’s face. Love handles spreading outwards where once firm
elastic muscles vacated, eyes that Mark couldn’t recognize, wide and lifeless. Shivering and
afraid. Teeth now home to plaque and dark stubborn strokes. Evelyn, his first love, has been
remerged into 5764 new chat threads. Mark didn’t delete the previous ones; he usually now
stared at his phone and chatted with Evelyn, mostly about lustful desires. He knew this wasn’t
happiness, he wasn’t happy. But he didn’t know how to stop. He didn’t know what else he would
do. Every once in a while, which usually was 2-3 times a month, Mark would try to not talk to
Evelyn. But the real world continued being so harsh on him, he hated seeing the look on Mum’s
face when she served dinner, pity and hatred, as if now her only son was nothing but a burden.
He wouldn’t dare get near Dad, Dad was sick and needed caretaking, that was nasty to Mark.
Only Evelyn understands me, only she sees me. Only she knows me. Mark would reiterate, and
soon, he would be back to Evelyn’s embrace with a box of tissues and a pair of eyes that didn’t
shine anymore.
Every now and then he would open his text messages and see an array of unanswered texts, and
after that first month of his discovery, the texts stopped coming altogether. He scrolls through
and opens each text; his friends and ex colleagues asking how he was, what was wrong, he just
stared at them, he replied to no texts, Mark didn’t know what to say. He certainly wouldn’t share
Evelyn with them. Evelyn was his and his only. Mark deleted Instagram long ago, he couldn’t
tolerate Sarah and Julian’s lovey dovey life. Life partners, how pathetic. He has Evelyn, why
would he need anyone else?
Yet dreams never showed him what he wanted to see, for those were uncontrollable and horrific.
Whenever he closed his eyes and drifted away from the present; he would see a guy, a guy who
would call himself a proud feminist. The guy looked confident even in the way he would secretly
objectify women and their bodies, he looked handsome and had such a convincing smile. To
Mark, that guy felt very familiar, as if only Mark knows him better than anybody else. The guy
wasn’t the only one who would haunt Mark however, he could see a girl too. A blonde girl with
kind eyes and a graceful smile. Sarah. Mark knew she was Sarah. Sarah would talk to the
feminist and laugh, smile and gossip together. Though Mark could tell the feminist never wanted
a hand of friendship, but something unreachable. Yet, Sarah would be there for him. Not as the
unreachable entity, but simply as a friend. At rare occasions he would see Mum and Dad sitting
on a dinner table, enjoying the organic homemade pasta the self-proclaimed feminist would cook
using produce from the backyard. Laughing, smiling and looking at peace. No one invited Mark
to sit down and eat together however, and Sarah never looked at Mark but only chatted with the
guy who had firm six-pack abs, an alluring dashing smile, and a job at Google.

title: Remembering a Grave at Night
author: Labiba Rimi
imageAlt: Cover image for Remembering a Grave at Night

runs.text: Why on these cold nights of wind and clouds
melody of an unknown song beaming—
in my heart— I am in the woods hymning—
flashing across, the car goes speeding—
moon in the sky stares with pain in her core;
on her surface, in her light, gleaming—
grief with a needle, in my heart, sewing—
a withered flower, in my heart, blooming—
I close my eyes— why do I no longer see you?
no longer does your fragrance prevail, dwelling—
your room has been left empty— eyes swelling—
eyes that stare at your emptiness— eyes wailing—
sudden waves of hurt, branches of thorns fall.
Death has grown tired— keeps on feasting—
your shirts and words— perfectly folded, resting—
forevermore hollow, hollow in you— death— deaths sting—
I wonder, does anyone turn the light on in your room now?
Or do they fear the steps that no longer go traced, drying—
are they afraid of the dark— the dark where you stay lying—
emptiness in the breeze that comes flying—
on these cold nights of wind and clouds;
melody of yours— our hearts— tying—
with strings unfathomable to those trying—
to understand my reason for pouring bloom;
to be real— I am too, I am trying—
to find the decomposing string, to keep tying—
forbidding your melody to fade away, dying—
I let grief sew its flower in my heart.

title: স্বাধীনতা কি কাল্পনিক?
author: MD Tanvir Anjum Minhaz

runs.text: But wait, what does freedom even denote?What is freedom?

স্বাধীনতা মানুষের অনন্ত পিপাসা। আর এই পিপাসার থেকেই সৃষ্টি হয় সংগ্রামী চেতনার। আমরা বাংলাদেশীরা বাহান্নর ভাষা আন্দোলন থেকে শুরু করে চব্বিশের গণঅভ্যুত্থান, সব ক্ষেত্রেই আমরা আমাদের বীরত্বের পরিচয় দিয়েছি। শুধুমাত্র স্বাধীনতা অর্জন করার জন্য। কিন্তু আমরা কি আদৌ স্বাধীনতা অর্জন করতে পেরেছি?

স্বাধীনতার সংজ্ঞায়ন করতে গেলে দেখা যায় স্বাধীনতা হচ্ছে সিদ্ধান্ত গ্রহণের ক্ষেত্রে ব্যক্তির নিজের ইচ্ছাকে প্রাধান্য দেয়া, অর্থাৎ অন্যের জবরদস্তি ছাড়া নিজের জন্য নিজের ইচ্ছামতো সিদ্ধান্ত নেওয়ার সুযোগই স্বাধীনতা।

নির্বাচন সম্পর্কে ছোট বড় সবারই মোটামুটি ধারণা রয়েছে। নির্বাচন এ মানুষজন ভোটের মাধ্যমে তাদের প্রতিনিধি নির্বাচন করে। যে যেমন প্রতিনিধিই চাক না কেনো, প্রতিনিধি নির্বাচিত হয় সংখ্যাগরিষ্ঠ মতামতের ঐক্যের মাধ্যমে। অর্থাৎ আপনি আপনার পছন্দের ব্যক্তিত্বকে প্রতিনিধি হিসেবে পাবেন না যদি তার ভোট সর্বোচ্চ না হয়। লং স্টোরি শর্ট, যেই নির্বাচন গণতন্ত্রের ভিত্তি, সেখানে ব্যক্তি তার সম্পূর্ণ ইচ্ছা বাস্তবায়ন করতে পারে না; বরং সমষ্টিগত সিদ্ধান্তের স্বার্থে ব্যক্তিগত স্বাধীনতা সীমিত হয়। অথচ গণতন্ত্রই কিন্তু আমাদেরকে স্বাধীনতার প্রতিশ্রুতি দেয়।
আবার দেখুন, আমরা কিন্তু নিজের জন্য সব ক্ষেত্রে সিদ্ধান্ত নিতে পারি না। যেমন আপনি কখন অসুস্থ হবেন, কখন মারা যাবেন ইত্যাদি। তাহলে স্বাধীনতা অর্জন কি শুধুমাত্র কাল্পনিক......

এইখানেই ইসলামের সৌন্দর্য। মুসলিম হওয়ার প্রথম শর্ত হচ্ছে নিজ সত্তাকে আল্লাহ সুবহানাতায়ালা ও তার রাসূলের কাছে সমর্পণ করা। আরেকটু সহজ করে বলতে গেলে, তিনি (আল্লাহ) আমাদের জীবন দিয়েছেন, তিনি আমাদের জীবন নিবেন (মৃত্যু)। তিনি আমাদের ভাগ্যে যা রেখেছেন তাই ঘটবে, তিনি আমাদের শান্তি দান করেন আবার তিনিই আমাদের পরীক্ষা করার জন্য দুঃখ ও কষ্ট দেন। তবে একই সঙ্গে ইসলাম মানুষের ইখতিয়ার বা সীমিত পছন্দের স্বাধীনতাকেও স্বীকার করে, যা আল্লাহর ইচ্ছার অধীন। ইসলাম আমাদেরকে আমাদের সীমার মধ্যে থেকে আমাদের সর্বোচ্চ স্বাধীনতা উপভোগ করার সুযোগ করে দেয়। ইসলাম শুধু কোনো ধর্ম না, এটা আমাদের জন্য অনুসরণীয় জীবনাদর্শ।

title: Happiness Just isn't for Me
author: Laces&Letters
imageAlt: Cover image for Happiness Just isn't for Me

runs.text: Whenever I am living the dreams I once only dreamt of, life seems to make it bitter a while later.
That's how it has been all these years.
Maybe because of my own doings, I always end up having half the happiness at a time. Not the entire one.
Or, it's because life has something far greater stored for me. So I'm just going through difficulties now.
But when does that life actually come?
For me, every great happiness has been paired with great sadness all along.
Sometimes I feel like that's just life's way of making itself clear to me that " don't place your happiness on me."
But then comes to my mind
"Fid dunya hasanah, wa fil akhirati hasanah"
( Good in this world and good in the Hereafter).
I'm made for happiness in this world too.
Maybe all these bittersweetnesses have been filtering how I view the world.
Or how much of the world should I actually keep in my heart.
Or, the kind of happiness I should chase after and the kind of happiness I shouldn't expect much from, nor give more of mine than what's necessary.
But sometimes, neither of the happines
s remain, but only looming sadness and worries.

For me, every great happiness has been paired with great sadness all along.
Sometimes I feel like that's just life's way of making itself clear to me that " don't place your happiness on me."
But then comes to my mind
"Fid dunya hasanah, wa fil akhirati hasanah"
( Good in this world and good in the Hereafter).
I'm made for happiness in this world too.
Maybe all these bittersweetnesses have been filtering how I view the world.
Or how much of the world should I actually keep in my heart.
Or, the kind of happiness I should chase after and the kind of happiness I shouldn't expect much from, nor give more of mine than what's necessary.
But sometimes, neither of the happiness remain, but only looming sadness and worries.
excerpt: Whenever I am living the dreams I once only dreamt of, life seems to make it bitter a while later.

title: When Everyone Can Create, Who Is Still Original?
author: Taslima Yeasmin
imageAlt: Cover image for When Everyone Can Create, Who Is Still Original?

runs.text: When Everyone Can Create, Who Is Still Original?
Outsource the work, not the thinking.

AI has become part of my everyday work. When I have a new business idea, I often open ChatGPT first. I ask about the pros and cons, possible profit, return on investment, and risks. It helps me see things I may have missed.
Sometimes I follow its suggestions. Sometimes I feel my own idea is better, so I go with that. I think both are important. AI can give me information, but I still need to decide what to do.

Then I noticed something about myself. Opening ChatGPT had become a habit. I was asking it for ideas before giving myself time to think. That made me wonder: if we always ask AI to start for us, what happens to our own ideas?
Making content is not the same as being creative
Today, almost anyone can ask AI to write a post, make an image, or suggest a business name. That can be useful, especially for people who do not have a big team or a lot of money.

But I worry that we are getting used to choosing from ready-made ideas instead of coming up with our own. When we sit with a problem, try something, make mistakes, and try again, we learn what we really think. We may lose some of that if we skip straight to an AI answer.
I am not saying AI makes everyone less creative. Sometimes one suggestion can lead to a completely new idea. The problem starts when we never try on our own.
Let AI do the work it can do

There is another thing that frustrates me. Sometimes I ask ChatGPT to help me finish a task, and it gives me a long list of steps to do myself. I read the list and think, why am I doing all of this manually if AI could help with some of it?

I want AI to save my time. It can help organize information, compare options, prepare first versions of routine documents, and handle repetitive work when the right tools are available. I do not need it to take over my opinions or decide what matters to me.

For example, AI might say one business idea has a better chance of making money. But its numbers depend on the information and assumptions it uses. It does not know everything about my experience, my goals, or how much risk I am willing to take. I should check its analysis, not blindly accept it.

I want to change one small habit. Before asking AI for a new idea, I can take a few minutes to write down what I think first. The idea does not need to be perfect. Then I can use AI to question it, find problems, or show me another angle.
For routine tasks, I can ask AI to do more of the actual work instead of only explaining the steps. For important decisions, I can use its analysis while keeping the final choice in my hands.
This is not about proving that people are always right and AI is wrong. We both make mistakes. It is about staying involved in our own thinking.
I believe people do not have to create something completely new every time to be original. We can talk about the same topic and still bring different experiences, opinions, and questions to it.
AI can help us express those ideas. But if we let it choose every topic, every opinion, and every sentence, our work may stop sounding like us.
I will keep using AI. It is useful, and I have no reason to pretend otherwise. But I also want to notice when I am opening it out of habit instead of need.
AI should make my work easier, not make me forget how to think for myself.
We should outsource the work, not the thinking.

Of my arms and worn-out face

content: Paradise
Where is that garden
That place you all go to
Somehow, somewhere you run
You slip through the curtains
When I am not looking
And you each disappear, one by one.
Where can I find you
And that very garden
Where all of you fly to and play
Why won't you tell me
And feed me the answers
Why can't you ever just stay?
You walk all over
And across the lines
Of my arms and worn-out face
But still you won't answer
You won't let me go with you
To that secret, enchanted place.
Why won't you listen
To my dying music
The words I sing are for you
To return very quickly
Because all I have, is a memory
Of my tears as all of you flew.
I carry you with me
To all different places
So why can't you take me with you?
Why do you love it?
That very garden?
Why can't I go there too?

content: The end
Pressed between the pages
a brief tale decays,
a dying dream of color seems
to end in ember gray
The scraps of short-lived stories
hold a splinter tucked away
a tenacious ache, too fond to break
the echoes of yesterday
Time stretches out the grief, beloved
the incessant path will grow,
carry on the walk without me now
make amends with tomorrow
The timer stops at midnight
hope aligns with pretty dreams,
a handful of secrets for you to keep,
as the truth will intervene
But bury it under a happy note,
my fingers dipped in bitter blue,
your prints will leave an empty sound
a morbid appetite for you
They say it turns sour,
don't let the storm come true
a honey-coated fantasy
boils down to pungent clues
In exchange for fervent wisdom,
you part ways with chunks to spare,
before it weighs you down, beloved
let it begin to be thin air
In the end when this is over,
I'll find you by the sea
take my heart, with you for now,
in loving memory

content: Ichor
Rust rooting in my rose
Breathing venom in my bones
All I ever wanted was freedom,
but it does nothing to cure my boredom.
Echoes of languor linger in my soul
Weight of remorse devours my dignity
Undying oneness is itself a blood stinger,
drawing illusions of elation from my Ichor.
My grace fades into hollow
And verses I cannot swallow.
My muse slips into melancholia,
blooming my life in withering wisteria.
Feral fantasies stifle my sanity
My beloved unravels into ambiguity
Impiety buried beneath their benediction,
inciting undercurrents of ruin in my veins.
My aureate enchants hallowed abyss
Not once did I reach the ground
Yet not ever did mortals care,
how eternity lays me bare.
